card.name: Words before a cause or contribution verb
card.fires_on: Small hedging or linking words (may, also, to, largely, likely, not) that come right after a possible cause and just before a verb like cause, contribute, be credited or lead to.

modes.label: Hedge after a cause
modes.description: A modal or hedge such as may or likely follows a proposed cause, before a verb about causing an effect.
modes.example: Researchers say an increase in childhood obesity<< may>> be one cause.

modes.label: Cause-attribution phrasing
modes.description: Words like believed to or largely credited that introduce the reason for an outcome.
modes.example: Habitat changes are believed<< to>> be the primary causes of decline for both

modes.label: Causality judgment in labels
modes.description: A word in a safety statement about whether a drug caused or should be linked to an event.
modes.example: determines that depo-subQ provera 104 did<< not>> cause the abnormalities.

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with contribute/contributing wording, as in 'may contribute to'.
